synopsis: ISO 21815-4 passed its FDIS ballot on 28 May 2026 and reached stage 60.00, “Under publication,” on 4 September 2026, with edition 1 scheduled for October 2026; the corpus recommends not citing it as published until its text appears [f2668, f2170, f1708, f2172]. It addresses swing-and-rotation risk areas and levels for earth-moving, underground-mining and road-construction machinery, with coverage described as objects between ground level and cabin top and explicit limitations concerning height and working tools [f1707, f1709, f11239]. Across chapters, it is described as covering motion inhibition before rotation starts while excluding collision avoidance through automatic braking, although two quoted scope statements also exclude “inhibit,” creating an unresolved wording tension [f2171, f3379, f15153, f1710, f7731]. Planning recommendations are to parameterize swing-risk geometry by machine model, track the forthcoming standard during validation, and include standards watching and re-baselining before design freeze [f6770, f2641, f15058]. The corpus reports no statistical sample-size or simulation-credibility rules in the listed standards and no located acceptance of simulation evidence; physical tests remain necessary under the ISO 21815 framework, but unavailable paid texts mean that failure to find simulation-replacement acceptance is not proof of prohibition [f6749, f11237, f8145, f7544]. Whether the final October text matches the quoted catalogue summary remains uncertain because the published text was not reviewed [f1965].
